headline: LCS Programme: RM8.3B Spent, First Ship in Sea Trials, Original Schedule 7 Years Late
context: PAC's 2022 report on the Littoral Combat Ship programme found RM6.08B paid against an original RM9.13B contract, since revised to RM11.2B for 5 vessels. MINDEF put spending at about RM8.3B in January 2026. No ship has been delivered; the first is now due in April 2027.

changes.summary: Correction: Rebuilt on PAC figures: RM6.08 billion spent against a RM9.13 billion contract, since revised to RM11.2 billion for five ships, with the first ship in sea trials. Removed an unverified 340% incursion figure.

Correction: MINDEF put LCS spending at about RM8.3 billion (74%) on 28 Jan 2026; earlier editions said RM6.08 billion, PAC's 2021 figure. The contract was awarded in Dec 2011 and signed in Jul 2014, not signed in 2011. The former BNS managing director's CBT charge ended in a DNAA on 12 Mar 2025.

cards.big: About RM8.3 billion spent. Zero ships delivered to the Royal Malaysian Navy. The first vessel is in sea trials.
cards.sub: LCS programme: awarded 2011, contract signed July 2014, first delivery due 2019. Original contract RM9.13B for 6 ships, revised to RM11.2B for 5 ships.

cards.big: PAC identified RM1.4B in cost overruns and allocations used for purposes other than the LCS works.
cards.sub: PAC also found payments exceeding actual work: 63.8% paid for the first ship against 42.7% of work done. The 2023 contract moved payments from milestones to progress of works.

cards.big: MACC sent investigation papers to the AGC in August 2022. The former BNS managing director was charged with CBT involving RM21M.
cards.sub: In March 2025 he got a discharge not amounting to acquittal (DNAA) after a hospital report found him unfit for trial. PAC also cited weak finances and direct negotiation.

cards.big: PAC and audit findings carry serious defence and maritime-enforcement implications. Patrol relies on MMEA, RMN assets and Op Naga.
cards.sub: AG reporting cited 89 Chinese-vessel incursions from 2016-2019. The LCS shortfall is one input into a broader capability picture.

cards.big: The question is no longer whether RM8.3B bought ships. It is whether the revised contract, new payment terms and trial timeline will close the gap they opened.
Like paying a builder RM6B against a RM9B contract, finding partial hulls instead of a delivered fleet, and renegotiating with the same builder.
cards.sub: Independent oversight came from PAC, the National Audit Department, MACC and auditors, not from BNS itself.

cards.big: Oversight did happen: PAC reports, declassification, a CBT charge that ended in a DNAA, a contract restructure. The unresolved test is delivery, now due April 2027.
